transcript: I actually have this test that I do, um, called the 4 second rule. So what I will do is I'll ask myself or I'll ask my staff members, if you were to look at your ads and you say like turned off all the copy, um, like the caption, sorry, and you were to turn off all the music, could you really understand in the first four seconds who this ad is for? What problem or desire it speaks to or solves and why they should keep watching? Now this isn't just to, I guess, test your hook. It's for you to understand if directly affects matters, understanding of who this ad is for in order to categorize it. So the one thing I see work with clients is reviewing that first 4 seconds before anything goes live. Specifically, obviously this is for our videos as mentioned, if they were to turn the sound off, turn off the captions, could you actually understand this? If the answer is no, you could add a written hook on there, not a fancy animated one. I've actually told my video editors now, stop making things animated, stop making them fancy. Have the hook on there. Make it clear, make it really clear who it is for, the problem or desire it solves. And that single change alone could dramatically improve your targeting accuracy on meta and also improve your results.
